class.name: Arm3D
class.brief_description: A procedural physical arm connecting a shoulder to a hand target.
class.description: Arm3D simulates three joints (shoulder, elbow, hand) using the same position-based solver as Rope3D. Assign two [Node3D] targets, the upper-arm and forearm lengths, and a shoulder-local elbow direction. The shoulder stays attached to its target and the hand follows its target within reach while the elbow responds to gravity, inertia, and its preferred pose. Use [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override] for the arm's material. Lengths and radius are measured in world units; scaling Arm3D does not change them. Shoulder orientation, including reflection, rotates the preferred elbow direction. Hand orientation does not affect the arm. The editor displays the target pose without running physics. The shoulder target and any enabled hand target must exist and be in the scene tree; otherwise the arm is hidden and simulation is reset. Disable [member hand_target_enabled] to let the elbow and hand swing freely under gravity, with only the shoulder pinned. This ignores the preferred elbow pose and initializes the arm at full length along gravity (world down when gravity is zero). The hand target is clamped to the reachable distance range, from the difference between segment lengths to their sum. Beyond full reach the arm becomes straight without growing. Targets too close to the shoulder produce a fully folded arm while preserving both segment lengths. The target node itself is never moved. At coincident targets, unequal lengths use the shoulder forward direction to choose the nearest reachable hand position; equal lengths fold along the elbow direction. These boundary poses bypass simulation to avoid competing constraints. When the bend direction is parallel to the shoulder-to-hand axis, the previous bend direction is projected onto the new plane, with a deterministic fallback if necessary. Simulation runs automatically on physics ticks, with bounded substeps and optional scene physics interpolation. Move targets before Arm3D's internal physics processing (for example, give the target controller an earlier [member Node.process_physics_priority]). After teleporting targets, call [method reset_simulation] to discard old velocities and interpolation history. This node generates a tube with rounded end caps. It does not drive a skeleton, move either target, or collide with the physics world.

method.name: apply_elbow_impulse
method.description: Applies a world-space impulse to the elbow. Has no effect before targets resolve or while simulation is disabled.

method.name: get_dropped_simulation_time
method.description: Returns accumulated seconds discarded by the substep budget since the last reset.

method.name: get_joint_positions
method.description: Returns the world-space shoulder, elbow, and hand positions, in that order. Returns an empty array when the targets are unavailable.

method.name: get_mesh
method.description: Returns the generated mesh. Treat it as read-only; Arm3D maintains its surfaces.

method.name: reset_simulation
method.description: Resamples both targets, restores the preferred elbow pose, and clears velocities, dropped time, and interpolation history. Call after teleporting the character or its targets.

members.member: Exponential velocity damping per second.
Nonzero preferred bend direction in the shoulder target's local orientation. Its magnitude is ignored.
Visual rounding from [code]0[/code] (a sharp joint) to [code]1[/code] (rounding across half of each segment). Does not add physical joints or alter simulation.
Spring stiffness in newtons per meter toward the preferred elbow position. Higher values resist displacement more strongly. Zero disables this pose constraint; segment lengths remain constrained.
Rest distance between elbow and hand, in world units.
World-space acceleration applied to the elbow and any unpinned hand.
If false, ignores the hand target without clearing its path. The hand and elbow simulate freely with fixed segment lengths; elbow stiffness is ignored. Changing this resets simulation.
Path to the [Node3D] defining the hand position. This target is not moved by Arm3D.
Maximum duration of one simulation substep in seconds.
Maximum substeps per physics tick. Excess time is discarded and reported by [method get_dropped_simulation_time].
Number of sides around the generated tube.

member.name: radius
member.deprecated: Use the individual segment radii instead.

members.member: Compatibility alias for older scenes and scripts. Setting this updates all four radii; reading it returns [member upper_arm_radius]. Hidden from the Inspector and omitted when saving scenes.
Radius at the shoulder in world units. The upper arm tapers linearly toward [member upper_arm_end_radius] along its length. Does not change the physical joints.

Radius the upper arm tapers toward at the elbow. Set lower than [member upper_arm_radius] to narrow toward the elbow, equal for constant thickness, or higher to widen. Blends into [member forearm_radius] over the rounded elbow, or over the nearest ten percent of each segment for a sharp elbow.
Radius at the elbow on the forearm side, in world units. The forearm tapers linearly toward [member forearm_end_radius] along its length.
Radius at the wrist, including the hand end cap. Set lower than [member forearm_radius] to narrow toward the wrist, equal for constant thickness, or higher to widen.
Path to the [Node3D] defining the shoulder position and elbow orientation.
If disabled, follows the target pose without inertia or gravity. Target tracking and rendering remain active.
Constraint iterations per substep. More iterations improve length constraint convergence at additional CPU cost.
Inverse stiffness of the length constraints. Zero resists stretching; larger values allow softer segments. Unreachable hand targets are clamped to the authored reach.
Total mass in kilograms, distributed half at the elbow and one quarter at each pinned endpoint.
Rest distance between shoulder and elbow, in world units.
